text:
**Yes, but only some models.** A portable power station works as a UPS for a computer only if it has documented UPS/EPS mode with automatic switchover. Many don't, and a basic one can cut power to your PC during an outage.

**What to check**
- **Transfer time:** Anker says a unit needs automatic switchover, a suitable transfer time, pure sine wave output, and safe pass-through operation ([Anker](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)). Pass-through charging alone isn't UPS protection ([Anker NAS guide](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)).
- **Whether your PC tolerates the gap:** EcoFlow warns that 20-30 ms switchovers can risk data loss ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). Anker is more measured: 10-20 ms works for some devices, but it isn't 0 ms, so check your device's manual. Both are manufacturers selling these products. Most desktop power supplies ride through short gaps, but I can't confirm that for your specific PC.
- **Wattage and runtime:** Add up your PC's real draw, ideally measured with a plug-in watt meter, and compare it to the unit's continuous output. Runtime is roughly Wh × 0.85 ÷ watts, and real-world runtime will be somewhat lower.
- **Shutdown signaling:** Standard UPS communication for automatic shutdown isn't guaranteed. Anker says to use an online double-conversion UPS if you need 0 ms transfer or UPS communication.

**Options from the results**
- [Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups): 2,010Wh, 1,500W pure sine wave, 10 ms UPS switchover, $699.99 after coupon per Anker's page.
- [EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply): 600W output, switchover under 10 ms, and EcoFlow's pick for a desktop plus external drives. The results didn't include a price.
- [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2): 2,073.6Wh, 2,600W, UPS switchover up to 15 ms, $899 ($854.05 with code AFF5OFF). That link is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. At up to 15 ms it's the slowest of the three.
- I'd skip EcoFlow's DELTA 3 models for this unless you verify their switchover time. The support pages in the results list the question but not the answer.

**Bottom line:** For a typical desktop, a unit with a 10 ms or faster documented UPS mode is reasonable. If your PC is critical, you want automatic shutdown, or your PC's manual requires 0 ms transfer, buy a dedicated online UPS instead. Either way, run a test by unplugging the wall power while the PC is on.
